clue.text: Discontinuance of South American payment

parts.note: S is the compass abbreviation for South
US is short for American, as in the US
a pension is a regular payment made to a retired person

explanation.surface: A remark about a South American payment being stopped.
explanation.definitionFit: A suspension is a halt or temporary stop, so it is a discontinuance.

clue.text: Arrange about can-opener for a party

indicators.note: about means one piece goes around the other, so the word for arrange is wrapped round a letter

parts.note: to set things is to arrange them

indicators.note: the opener of can is its first letter, the one that starts the word

explanation.surface: Someone setting out a can-opener ready for a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A sect is a faction or group, a party within a larger body of believers.

clue.text: Trim figure without fruit?

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the word for figure stands round the fruit

parts.note: a figure is a body's shape
hips are the red fruit of the wild rose

explanation.surface: A dieter asks whether a trim figure is possible without eating fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Shipshape means neat and in good order, as a trim boat is.

clue.text: The name of the shrub is Greybeard

explanation.surface: A gardener announcing that a certain bush is called Greybeard.
explanation.definitionFit: The elder is a common shrub with white flowers and black berries; an elder is also an old man of authority, a greybeard.

clue.text: A composer reduced to tears in composing

indicators.note: composing means putting together afresh, so the letters of tears in are set out anew

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A composer so moved by his own work that he is reduced to tears.
explanation.walkthrough: John Stainer was a Victorian English composer of church music. 'composing' rearranges TEARS IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir John Stainer was an English composer, known for The Crucifixion.

clue.text: Some envoys' terseness angers the natives

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Diplomats' curt manner irritates the local people.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'angers the natives' is wrong: only 'the natives' defines; 'angers' is a link joining the surface. Natives are oysters raised in British waters, notably Whitstable and Colchester.
explanation.definitionFit: Natives is the trade name for oysters bred in British beds, as opposed to imported ones.

clue.text: Over and above what local sources can provide

indicators.note: the words local sources can provide some of their own letters, a run lying across them

explanation.surface: A remark on what extra can be supplied by local suppliers.
explanation.definitionFit: Also means in addition, besides, which is what over and above means.

clue.text: Cut a large number in the rural way

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another, the number going within the country road

parts.note: a lane is a narrow country road
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Advice to cut down a large number of things in the country manner.
explanation.definitionFit: To lance is to cut open, as a surgeon lances a boil.

clue.text: Upset the open vase by little Edward

parts.note: overt means open, not hidden
an urn is a kind of vase
Ed is a short form of the name Edward

explanation.surface: Someone knocking over an open vase standing by a small boy named Edward.
explanation.definitionFit: Overturned means knocked over or upset, as a capsized boat is.

clue.text: Pair with a monstrous woman and get on!

parts.note: an ogress is a female ogre

explanation.surface: An instruction to team up with a fearsome woman and make headway.
explanation.definitionFit: To progress is to advance or make headway, to get on in life.

clue.text: A youngster admonished for carrying cash

indicators.note: carrying means the first word holds the other inside it

parts.note: chid is an old past tense of chide, to scold or admonish
L stands for pounds, British money, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A young person told off for having money on them.
explanation.walkthrough: CHID is the archaic past tense of chide.
explanation.definitionFit: A child is a young person, a youngster.

clue.text: Profession offering security

explanation.surface: A career that provides financial safety.
explanation.definitionFit: An assurance is a solemn declaration or profession of something; it is also a pledge giving security, and in Britain a word for life insurance.

clue.text: Make foreign sergeant wild

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters of sergeant running out of control into a new order

explanation.surface: A sergeant driven wild by a foreign posting.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange is to alienate, to make a person a stranger or foreign to another.

clue.text: The visitor's supposed to be heard

indicators.note: to be heard says the word for supposed is listened to, not read

parts.note: to have guessed is to have supposed

explanation.surface: A visitor is expected to make himself heard.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe s is 'is': 'The visitor is' a word that sounds like 'supposed'.
explanation.definitionFit: A guest is a visitor received in someone's home.

clue.text: Discipline cheat-an employee

parts.note: to take someone in is to deceive or cheat them
a hand is a worker, as on a farm or ship

explanation.surface: A firm deciding to punish a worker who cheated.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone in hand is to bring them under control, to discipline them.

clue.text: A mature settled layman

indicators.note: settled means the letters come to rest in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A grown-up, settled person who is not a professional.
explanation.definitionFit: An amateur is a non-professional, someone who is a layman in a field.

clue.text: Charm will ensure admission

explanation.surface: A promise that a lucky charm guarantees getting in.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrance (stress on the second syllable) is to charm or bewitch; an entrance (stress on the first) is a way in, an admission.

clue.text: Narrow old money lender

parts.note: S stood for a shilling in Britain's pre-decimal money
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tight-fisted moneylender of former times.
explanation.walkthrough: S was the abbreviation for the shilling, a British coin before 1971.
explanation.definitionFit: Slender means thin, so a slender margin is a narrow one.

clue.text: Exhibitionist exciting dread with evil

indicators.note: exciting means stirring up, so the letters of dread and evil are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A show-off thrilling people with fear and wickedness.
explanation.definitionFit: A daredevil is a reckless person who shows off with risky stunts.

clue.text: Hellenic heroine chosen to lead fighting men

indicators.note: to lead means the first piece goes in front of the second

parts.note: elect means chosen, as in the president-elect
RA is the Royal Artillery, British gunners

explanation.surface: A Greek heroine picked to command an army.
explanation.definitionFit: Electra is a figure of Greek tragedy, daughter of Agamemnon, who avenged her father.

clue.text: Cupidity, a shortcoming holding the painter up

indicators.note: holding means the word for a failing contains the reversed artist

parts.note: a vice is a moral failing or shortcoming

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a painter

explanation.surface: Greed, a failing that keeps an artist on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns RA into AR, which goes inside VICE after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice is extreme greed for wealth, the same as cupidity.

clue.text: Book put by for a rainy day?

definitions.text: put by for a rainy day?

explanation.surface: A book saved to read when it rains.
explanation.definitionFit: To reserve is to book a seat or room; a reserve is also money or supplies kept back against future need.

clue.text: Is surrounded by telephones, so revolts

indicators.note: surrounded by means the first piece sits inside the second

parts.note: to ring someone is to telephone them, so rings means telephones

explanation.surface: Someone besieged by ringing phones who finally rebels.
explanation.definitionFit: Risings are uprisings or rebellions, revolts against authority.

clue.text: A woman of Roman origin

indicators.note: of Roman origin says the name is made from the letters of Roman

explanation.surface: A remark that a certain lady is descended from Romans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of Roman origin' looks like ancestry, but the name comes from rearranging ROMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Norma is a woman's given name, also the heroine of Bellini's opera.

clue.text: Sack incompetent flier

indicators.note: incompetent suggests the word flier is handled badly and comes out muddled

explanation.surface: Fire a pilot who can't fly properly.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle a place is to ransack or plunder it, to sack it.

clue.text: Doesn't stay, so doesn't get justice

explanation.surface: Someone who leaves and so escapes punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Absconding is leaving secretly, and in particular fleeing to escape arrest or trial, so escaping the law.

clue.text: It's OK for a Greek character to be beast

parts.note: pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Approval for a Greek person to play an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The okapi is an African animal related to the giraffe.

clue.text: Unfortunately yielding to the Parisian skinhead

parts.note: a la is French for to the

indicators.note: the head of skin is its first letter

explanation.surface: Sadly giving way to a French skinhead.
explanation.definitionFit: Alas is an exclamation of regret, used where one might say unfortunately.

clue.text: Love may be seen as a disease

explanation.surface: Love seen as an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Affection is fondness or love; in medicine an affection is also a disease or disorder of the body.

clue.text: Basic forging equipment

parts.note: forging hints at faking documents, but here it is the smith's work: the fundamental item on which hot metal is hammered

explanation.surface: Essentials for a forger's workshop.
explanation.definitionFit: The block on which a blacksmith hammers metal is the most basic tool of the forge.

clue.text: An action that can be reversed

indicators.note: the word for the act reads the same backwards as forwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A legal note about a decision that can be overturned.
explanation.definitionFit: A deed is something done, an act or action.

clue.text: Poetry about a queer French place

indicators.note: about means the poetry wraps round the rest

parts.note: verses are lines of poetry
queer in its old sense of unwell, feeling ill

explanation.surface: Poems written about an eccentric French town.
explanation.definitionFit: Versailles is a town near Paris, famous for Louis XIV's palace.
